description_short.value: Ghanaian publisher of school textbooks, delisted from the Ghana Stock Exchange on 14 April 2023 after it stopped operating.
description_short.source: Written by us from GSE PR 102/2023 (notice of compulsory delisting of Sam-Woode Limited) and the Sam-Woode Limited 2018 Annual Report (GSE PR 253/2019, note 1: educational publisher, printer and seller of educational books and material)

description_full.value: Sam-Woode Ltd is a Ghanaian educational publisher that developed, printed and sold textbooks and other teaching materials. It is no longer listed: the Ghana Stock Exchange suspended its shares on 29 September 2020 and compulsorily delisted the company on 14 April 2023. It listed in April 2002. Sales fell from GHS 2.0 million in 2017 to GHS 1.05 million in 2018 and, unaudited, GHS 0.45 million in 2019. It made losses in each of those years, and by the end of 2019 its liabilities exceeded its assets by GHS 0.9 million. Its auditor had drawn attention to the going-concern assumption in the 2018 accounts. A rights issue to fund a digital transformation programme stalled and was cancelled; shareholders approved raising GHS 3 million through a corporate bond instead. In 2018 the company moved its head office from Dansoman to Nyanyano, near Kasoa, where it set up a print-on-demand press. At the annual general meeting of 21 November 2019, shareholders voted to delist voluntarily. In 2020 the company suspended operations, because the new Ghana Education Service curriculum had made its textbook stock obsolete and stopped its book sales. It planned to restructure into a parent company with two subsidiaries: SWL Learn, an online learning app, and SWL Edutech, a printing business. It never completed the voluntary delisting, so the GSE delisted it. Its last dividends were GHS 0.004 a share for 2014 and GHS 0.012 for 2015. In 2018 its chairman, Kwesi Sam-Woode, held 24.74% of the shares.
